verdict.rationale: Semgrep documents taint-tracking rules for catching injection bugs. It also documents cross-file (interfile) analysis that detects vulnerabilities across files and folders, and interprocedural, interfile data-flow (constant propagation) in Semgrep AppSec Platform. Together these cover tracing taint across file and function boundaries, though the docs never state explicitly that taint mode itself is interprocedural, and the cross-file capability appears tied to the platform rather than the plain CLI. missing for 10: an explicit first-party statement that taint tracking itself runs interprocedurally and across files, detail on how cross-function taint behaves (sources/sinks/sanitizers across calls), and independent or hands-on corroboration of cross-file taint findings.

support.subject: As a security-engineer, I can detect taint-style vulnerabilities that flow across files and function boundaries

citations.quote: Taint tracking (known also as taint analysis) enables you to write simple rules that catch complex injection bugs, such as those that can result in cross-site scripting (XSS).
Semgrep supports taint analysis, also known as taint tracking, through taint rules.
To turn on cross-file analysis, which allows you to detect vulnerabilities across files and folders
Semgrep AppSec Platform supports interprocedural (cross-function), interfile (cross-file) constant propagation.
scan your project for security issues using Semgrep Code’s interfile analysis
